summary: Bunzai remote access is off by default and host-managed in Settings. Tailscale gates the private link by the owner's numeric account identity; LAN requires a random code and host approval. Separate authenticated loopback listeners and host-only routes preserve management authority. Supported packaged builds embed their compile target's Go helper. Startup verifies target, size and SHA-256 before atomic extraction to a digest-specific per-user cache. Valid cached bytes are reused; damaged cache is repaired from verified embedded bytes. Packaged helper selection accepts only that prepared path, even after preparation failure; neighboring files, source paths and downloaded caches cannot replace it. Preparation makes no network request, starts no process and changes no setting. Failure leaves local Studio and LAN usable. Source checkouts retain deliberate developer helper locations and optional pinned downloads. Older release recovery assets remain available at their original URLs; new normal releases publish apps and checksums. OpenSSL resolves through PATH or standard Git for Windows directories, and LAN operation errors are visible. Source, mocked-boundary, live and packaged evidence retain explicit limits.

sections.title: Containers and SSH forwarding
sections.summary: Container or headless use does not need a browser inside that environment. The bunzai ui startup receipt prints the local Studio URL, one copyable SSH command for the Studio port, and when the isolated Lua regex listener started a second forward for its random sandbox port. Run it on the browser machine, replace user@server, keep the tunnel open, browse localhost with the printed ui-port. Browsing the server or container IP is refused by the trusted Host gate. HTML may arrive before api/settings is refused, so the browser turns that 403 into localhost and SSH instructions with Studio, Settings Remote access deep link, and one-port recovery copy buttons; host-only API gates still decide whether controls may change anything. One-port is enough for ordinary Studio work; Lua and regex benches need both ports because ADR-009 uses a second ephemeral loopback origin. Tailscale and LAN serve the approved Studio surface only and do not make the sandbox listener a general remote endpoint. This does not broaden hostAllowed, expose a new listener, or weaken token and Origin checks.

sections.title: Two listeners, one trust boundary
sections.summary: The trusted loopback listener defaults to port 8321 and requires the existing Host, Origin and session-token checks. Each Studio instance also binds its own ephemeral private loopback listener for the Tailscale helper. The actual bound address is passed to that helper, and every proxied request must carry the instance-specific per-boot CSPRNG secret. The secret travels through the child environment rather than argv and is refused by the trusted door. Another instance secret cannot authenticate this listener. A failed private bind leaves mesh unavailable while local Studio and LAN remain usable. Failed main-listener startup releases its already-created private listener, and closing before saved settings resolve prevents a later automatic mesh restart. LAN retains port 8790 and reports occupied-port failure rather than attaching to another app.
topics: untrusted 127.0.0.1 on an instance-owned ephemeral port

sections.title: The Tailscale owner gate
sections.summary: The sidecar embeds Tailscale via tsnet and for every remote request calls WhoIs on the caller tailnet address, admitting only the studio owner's own account. Identity is compared by numeric user id who.UserProfile.ID equals Self.UserID via resolveOwnerID and newProxy; login-name strings are not used because tsnet can return an empty login for the owner node while the numeric id is populated. Fail closed everywhere: unresolved owner id zero denies everyone; unidentifiable caller with no WhoIs is denied; a caller whose node has no stable id is denied because a device that cannot be tracked or kicked will not be served. Identity headers forwarded upstream X-Tailscale-User and X-Tailscale-Node are taken from WhoIs never from client-supplied headers so a forged header cannot survive. These properties are unit-tested against a fake resolver in sidecar main_test.go.

sections.title: The LAN gate: connect code + per-device approval
sections.summary: LAN access requires a random Argon2-hashed connect code and separate host approval. Wrong guesses use per-IP exponential backoff; pending sessions expire after fifteen minutes and have per-IP limits. The listener uses self-signed TLS with LAN and loopback subject alternative names, and the owner verifies the fingerprint. Approval cookies require Secure, HttpOnly, SameSite Lax and Path slash: HTTPS-only listening does not stop a plaintext request to another port from exposing an insecure cookie. Login JSON caps at 1024 bytes and code input at 32 characters. Admission reserves one verification per IP and four globally before await, with bounded attempt and session stores. Reset immediately invalidates old credentials and generations; only current comparisons can issue sessions. Disabling invalidates pending startup, and expired sessions are swept before capacity checks. Browser certificate compatibility cannot justify removing Secure.

children.title: Session transport and bounded admission
children.summary: The session cookie requires Secure and HttpOnly with SameSite Lax and Path slash. A browser that cannot retain a Secure cookie must fail closed. The login route bounds JSON and code length; verification has synchronous per-IP and global admission without an unbounded queue. Attempt and session counts are capped, with expiry swept before admitting a session. Reset generations invalidate old hashes, comparisons and issuance immediately, and disabling LAN also invalidates pending listener startup. These are transport and admission protections rather than a measured browser compatibility guarantee.

sections.title: Host-only surface
sections.summary: Remote and LAN handlers refuse host management: remote-access controls, opening browsers, shutdown, restart and settings writes. Export-folder creation and file uploads are host-only because they write to the host disk; remote clients download locally instead. Bounded exclusive export writes preserve finished artifacts when a request is refused, remove only their own incomplete files and reject cancellation before opening. The same local token and origin checks still govern host requests.

sections.title: Kicking a device
sections.summary: The owner can remove any connected device from the host. Over Tailscale the app writes a kick command to the sidecar stdin; the sidecar blocklists that node stable id and denies it on the next request even though it is the owner own account via deviceTracker in main.go. On LAN the session is dropped.

sections.title: Where the sidecar binary comes from
sections.summary: Supported desktop and CLI builds embed the helper selected by their compile target in SIDECAR_TARGETS. Missing assets fail the build, and the generated file-loader module returns to a null placeholder after compilation. Startup verifies target, size and SHA-256, then atomically extracts into a digest-specific per-user path. Valid cached bytes are reused; damaged bytes are replaced only with verified embedded bytes. Packaged mode comes from the existing packaged-assets owner and survives failed preparation. The packaged resolver accepts only the prepared verified path, never source, sibling, PATH or optional downloaded-cache candidates. This prevents an extracted neighboring archive from supplying an executable helper. Preparation changes no settings, makes no network request and starts no process. Failed preparation leaves local Studio and LAN usable and exposes repair guidance without a dead helper-download action. Source runs retain repository, deliberate sibling and downloaded-cache locations. Public startup regressions use temporary files and mocked spawn without executing an arbitrary helper.

sections.title: The aux package: fetching the helper on request
sections.summary: Separate helper assets remain a recovery path for source checkouts and older apps. Current packaged apps use only their included verified helper and do not offer a separate helper download; their endpoint rejects that action. New normal releases publish app executables and checksums only, while older v0.1.53 recovery assets remain at their original URLs so existing pins keep working. Source recovery downloads require explicit host action, committed SHA-256 pins, bounded HTTPS fetching and the GitHub redirect allowlist. Verification precedes atomic installation. Downloaded helpers are not rehashed before every source-run spawn, and build hashes do not create a staleness warning. The panel reports availability without claiming which release supplied an overriding source helper. Pins cover Windows x64 and Linux x64/ARM64, with no macOS helper asset. Downloading does not enable mesh. Embedded build metadata remains separate from published recovery-download pins.

sections.title: Sidecar lifecycle
sections.summary: The mesh helper uses stdio for status and commands, and its parent-watch exits when stdin closes. The manager terminates only the child handle it launched, never all processes sharing an executable name. It ignores late output from a stopped child. LAN startup is coalesced and checked against a lifecycle generation, so a listener returned after Off is stopped immediately. Windows GUI-subsystem builds and hidden spawn windows avoid console flashes while preserving pipe handles. This audit verifies those ownership rules in isolated tests and source, without rerunning native packaged or real LAN operation.

sections.title: What is proven
sections.summary: Unit tests cover the Tailscale owner gate, LAN code formatting, per-IP throttle, approval limits and expiry, trusted-port secret refusal, host-only routes and unavailable helper behavior. The helper resolver has earlier compiled-path evidence. Download tests cover checksum mismatch, truncation, redirect policy and body limits; pin-format tests reject duplicate digests and constrain assets. Release tests assert workflow shape and platform coverage, while successful cross-builds require a real release. Earlier LAN and Tailscale journeys had live evidence, but the October 30 Secure-cookie, capped login, hash-concurrency, reset-generation and startup-revocation changes have only isolated handler and lifecycle regressions. They have not been reverified with a browser, real LAN or packaged host. This distinction prevents older live evidence from being attributed to the changed authentication implementation.

sections.title: Local-access certificate dependency and failures
sections.summary: Local network access uses installed OpenSSL to create its self-signed HTTPS certificate. Discovery checks PATH first and standard Git for Windows usr/bin and mingw64/bin locations on Windows. It downloads or installs no certificate executable. Missing OpenSSL produces installation guidance and allows retry. Generation and fingerprint failures remain errors, and the card displays failures from enable, disable, approval, denial and removal operations. Connect codes, explicit device approval and host-only management remain required. The isolated TLS regression starts an ephemeral real HTTPS listener, checks its IP SAN and fingerprint, verifies an unapproved request stays gated, and stops the listener. This is source listener evidence; it does not verify installed binaries or physical devices.
